newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money slips as CB stops borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money slips as CB stops borrowing.

text.p: Manila overnight money slipped to an average of 10.03125 percent on Tuesday from 10.0625 percent after the Central bank closed again its overnight borrowing facility and withdrew its two-day term reverse repos, traders said.
That left the market very liquid, they said.
Done rates were from 10.5 to 10.03125 percent, with 37 lenders and 21 borrowers.
Dealers said interest rates may rise next week as banks cover reserve positions for the long Easter holidays.
Meanwhile, the secondary market of T-bills saw quiet trading as banks awaited news on possible changes in U.S. interest rates which may be announced later on Tuesday.
A hike in U.S. interest rates may result in higher domestic rates to maintain the peso's premium over the U.S. dollar, traders said.
Banks were mostly buying the three-month bills to meet clients' requirements.
A Reuter poll of seven banks gave bid rates of 9.69 to 9.75 percent on three-month billls.
